newsitem.title: USA: SEC subpoenaes Fulton, Cty, Ga., bond documents.
newsitem.headline: SEC subpoenaes Fulton, Cty, Ga., bond documents.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission requested documents from Fulton County, Ga., bond issues, including a 1992 water-sewer refunding issue, the county disclosed in bond documents.
Calls to the county were referred to an attorney who has been unavailable for comment. SEC officials declined to comment.

But in a Nov 20 preliminary offering statement for Fulton's upcoming $3 million general obligation bond issue, the county said it had voluntarily provided to the SEC documents related to the $163.375 million water and sewer refunding.
The county said the documents involved, among other things, "the criteria used for evaluating and selecting underwriters and other participants (including financial advisors and various counsel.)"
The county said the SEC inquiries were captioned "In the Matter of Certain Securities Offerings by Florida and Georgia Issuers."
The Fulton inquiry appears to be linked to an SEC probe of bonds issued in Jacksonville, Fla. and surrounding Duval County, Fla.

Issuers there confirmed last month that the SEC had subpoenaed documents related to the selection of financial advisers and underwriters foR refunding bond issues by the Jackonsville Electric Authority and the Duval County School Board, as well as campaign contribution records for two school members.
The common thread in the issues appears to be Lazard Freres & Co, which, except for some advisory work, left the municipal bond business in December 1995.

Lazard was senior manager for the April 1992 Duval County School Board issue mentioned in the Florida subponae adn for the Fulton County water-sewer issue. The firm acted as financial adviser to the Jackonsville Electric Authority for 1992 and 1993 issues that were also cited in the Florida subponae.
A spokesman for Lazard said the company had no comment.
